clue.text: Presenter, an American politician, in for a difficult time with guitarist

parts.note: a disc jockey presents a radio show
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A broadcaster and a US politician face a rough patch alongside a guitar player.
explanation.walkthrough: DJ + AN + GORE + IN + HARD + T gives DJANGO REINHARDT; 'in for a difficult time' reads like an idiom but is three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Django Reinhardt was the Belgian-born Romani jazz musician famed for gypsy-swing playing on six strings.

clue.text: Cultivated pond with rows of blossom

indicators.note: cultivated ground is dug over and rearranged, so the letters get turned over

explanation.surface: A tended garden pond lined with rows of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The snowdrop is a small white flower that blooms in late winter, so it is an example of blossom.

clue.text: Wild about the foreign judge

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the pieces are read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper over a judge from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A feral animal has returned to an untamed state, living like a creature of nature.

clue.text: Knowledge penetrates falsehood and points to true image

indicators.note: to penetrate is to break into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: two compass points, S and S

explanation.surface: Understanding cuts through deceit and indicates the real picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' is plural, so two compass points are needed; both here are south.
explanation.definitionFit: A likeness is a portrait or representation that faithfully resembles its subject.

clue.text: Vouch for a team's first match

indicators.note: the first of the word team means only its opening letter is wanted

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Someone confirms the details of a side's opening fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or certify that something is true, the same as vouching.

clue.text: Jealous Othello, perhaps, retired thither?

parts.note: green with envy; jealousy is the green-eyed monster

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is read in the backward direction

parts.note: Othello is the Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: The jealous Othello leaves the stage to rest offstage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: an actor playing Othello retires to that room between scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: The green room is the backstage lounge where performers wait and relax when not on stage.

clue.text: Ladies' padding creates hubbub

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a frame worn under a Victorian skirt to puff out the back
second meaning: busy commotion and activity

explanation.surface: Women's padded clothing causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a nineteenth-century skirt support and noisy energetic activity.

clue.text: Major retailer to leave with guide, taking the way east

parts.note: to depart is to go away

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it within, so a piece goes inside

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A big shop's boss walks out with an adviser, heading east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The way' is a street, which crosswords shorten to its address abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A department store is a large shop selling many kinds of goods in separate sections, a big retail business.

clue.text: Member of sect on New Year's Day receiving Oriental coin

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: January 1st, with the digit 1 read as the letter I
the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries

explanation.surface: A religious follower gets a coin from the East as a New Year gift.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 in the date doubles as the letter I, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jansenists were a seventeenth-century Catholic movement following Cornelius Jansen's teaching on grace.

clue.text: Make up for scoundrel get-ting his innards in a twist

indicators.text: get-ting his innards in a twist
indicators.note: a twist scrambles the order, and innards limits it to the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A villain gets flustered while putting on cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the inner three letters are rearranged; the first and last stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouge is red cosmetic powder applied to the cheeks, one kind of facial cosmetic.

clue.text: Different crowd at the old jail

parts.note: new means not the same as before
the gate is the paying attendance at a sports match

explanation.surface: A fresh crowd gathers outside a historic prison.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWGATE was London's notorious prison, demolished in 1904.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate was a famous London prison for centuries, now gone, so it is a former place of confinement.

clue.text: Avenger divinely ordained by god

parts.note: the elect are those chosen by God

explanation.surface: An avenging figure claims a sacred mandate from a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek tragedy Electra helps her brother Orestes kill their mother to revenge their murdered father Agamemnon.

clue.text: Vegetables turned the boat round

definitions.note: plural; okra is used as a mass noun

indicators.note: something turned faces the opposite way, so the vessel's word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Greens loaded on a vessel that has turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is a green pod eaten as a vegetable, also called ladies' fingers.

clue.text: Live for a limited period under canvas and make progress

indicators.note: being under canvas means inside a shelter, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a term is a fixed span of time

explanation.surface: Camping for a while as a way of improving oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: Living under canvas means camping, so the canvas here is a tent rather than a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Betterment means improvement, an advance to a superior state, which is what progress is.

clue.text: Something like a thousand pounds raised during weird encounter

indicators.note: happening during an event means within it, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: a seance is a spooky meeting with spirits
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: in a down clue something raised reads upward, i.e. backwards

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for pounds weight

explanation.surface: A huge sum of money appears during a spooky gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A semblance is an outward appearance or resemblance, a thing that is similar to something else.

clue.text: Articulate at high speeds

definitions.meaning: second meaning: fast, as a fast train or delivery

explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' looks like an adjective but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to put thoughts into words, and also describes something sent or travelling fast.

clue.text: Harp on about deceased, or about their intentions

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to prate is to talk on tediously

explanation.surface: Someone goes on and on about a dead person and what they wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Probate is the legal proving of a will, the document recording what a dead person intended to happen to their estate.

clue.text: Illicitly accept currency in silver

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the money goes inside

parts.note: the ecu was the old European currency unit

explanation.surface: Taking cash in silver under the table.
explanation.definitionFit: To peculate is to embezzle, taking funds entrusted to one's care for personal use.

clue.text: Agreement about letter — concealing note without hiding it?

indicators.note: about means around, so the yes-word wraps the rest

parts.note: ay, a variant of aye, means yes

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hold it hidden within

parts.note: a vowel is a kind of letter

explanation.surface: A yes about a letter that hides a note, though nothing is hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a playful paraphrase of 'openly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Avowedly means openly declared, by one's own admission, so nothing is kept secret.

clue.text: Sort of mollusc that can scratch and rub chin

indicators.note: scratching messes up a surface, suggesting letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A sea creature able to scratch and rub its chin.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudibranchs are sea slugs, shell-less gastropods, which belong to the mollusc group.

clue.text: The old finish behind the young beginner — it's not very exciting

definitions.note: a clause standing for an adjective

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter
the beginner of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An old runner finishes behind a young novice in a dull race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old finish' looks like a phrase about age; it means the last letter of 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary means dull and depressing, lacking anything to stimulate interest.

clue.text: Where Othello strove for love-apple

indicators.note: striving means struggling, and struggling letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the shape of O

explanation.surface: The Moor fought to win a tomato.
explanation.walkthrough: In his final speech Othello recalls striking down a Turk 'in Aleppo once'; a love-apple is an old name for a tomato.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleppo is the Syrian city that Shakespeare's Othello names as a place he once fought.

clue.text: Army entertainer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large multitude, as in a heavenly multitude
second meaning: one who receives guests

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a soldier who performs; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a great throng or armed force and a person who receives guests at home.

clue.text: Get goat for two years

wordplay.note: anno is Latin 'in the year', and Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated by a wait of a couple of years.
explanation.definitionFit: To get someone's goat is an idiom meaning to irritate or exasperate them.

clue.text: Means of displaying pictures from top gallery

parts.note: the Tate is a group of British art galleries

explanation.surface: Showing artworks taken from a leading museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetate is clear film used for transparencies, laid on an overhead projector to show images on a screen.

clue.text: Easy-going Tenniel creation

indicators.note: a creation is something made up, so the name's letters are newly made into another word

parts.note: John Tenniel, illustrator of Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A relaxed figure drawn by the Alice illustrator.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means tolerant and mild, not strict, which matches a relaxed, easy-going nature.

clue.text: Scottish medic gets religion

indicators.note: getting something means taking it into one's possession, so it goes inside

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, a school subject

explanation.surface: A doctor from Scotland finds faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Doric is the dialect of north-east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric names the broad Scots speech of Aberdeenshire, so as an adjective it describes things from that region.

clue.text: Literature for a misguided drug user?

definitions.text: Literature for a misguided drug user?

parts.note: surface reading: reading matter for an addict
setter's reading: someone who cooks cannabis in a kettle rather than smoking it

explanation.walkthrough: Pot is slang for cannabis; the answer is also a hack novel written only to pay the bills.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a mediocre book churned out quickly for money, so it is a type of literature.
